constraints: Also usable purely to validate that a string is well-formed JSON (a parsing error is thrown otherwise).
If pointers were serialized, JSON Stringify must have been used to produce jsonString before calling JSON Parse.
Real values must fall within ±10.421e±10; text values must have all special characters (including quotes) escaped.
By default (type omitted), 4D infers the type from the target field/variable if one is defined, else infers it from the JSON value itself.

Date strings in "YYYY-MM-DD" format are returned as date values automatically when the database's date setting is Date type (the default); the 'Dates inside objects' setting of SET DATABASE PARAMETER controls whether JSON date strings are treated as local time or GMT.
Time values are parsed from numbers, interpreted by default as a number of seconds.

The * parameter is honored only when the returned value is of the object type; if passed, the result gains an extra __symbols property giving each property/sub-property's path, line number, and line offset -- useful for debugging, ignored for non-object results.

overloadMerges.note: Added sentinelValues to the 'type' param documenting the named 'Field and Variable Types' theme constants used to force a specific interpretation of the parsed value.

params.name: type
params.description: Forces the type to convert the parsed value into (Field and Variable Types theme constant).
If the parsed value is an object, adds a __symbols property with line position and offset of each property; ignored otherwise.

overloadMerges.semanticRole: Deserializes a JSON-formatted string into a 4D value (object, collection, or scalar), optionally forcing the result's type and optionally attaching source-position debug metadata.
